answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable stake before entering a market, then slash that stake when independently verified evidence shows coordinated fraud. A quill agent might flag a sparrow account, but flags alone do not trigger penalties: the rule needs evidence and an appeal, so honest newcomers are not punished for resemblance. An onyx-sized cluster of fake accounts must therefore lock up capital in every identity and risks losing it, making a Sybil swarm costly rather than free.
